title: Embryo contact versus soluble embryo signals
issue: The encoded input is physical contact, but the only cited experiment manipulates soluble signals and explicitly acts before contact.
conflicting: none identified; this is a scope mismatch, not a contradiction
current: E_CDH1_APICAL = IN_EMBRYO_CONTACT (an exact alias; the node computes nothing of its own)
proposed: Let IN_HCG and/or IN_EMBRYO_CONDITIONED_SIGNAL drive E_CDH1_APICAL, keeping contact as a separate requirement downstream
new_nodes: no; two declared inputs already exist and are unread
affects: topology and semantics; no rate or readout change
impact: E_CDH1_APICAL would stop being an alias of IN_EMBRYO_CONTACT and could become observable; currently clamping it changes no output in any state
strength: one human study, carcinoma-line maternal surface and spheroid surrogate
observability: not observable at baseline today (clamp changes nothing)
identifiability: would need the contact-held-constant comparison the source does not run
readiness: specification needed; not implementable from current evidence alone

title: Compartment-specific GP130/STAT3
issue: Epithelial and stromal STAT3 are separately required in mouse; the model has one epithelial pathway node.
supporting: REF-031 (Hiraoka 2020, epithelial Stat3-eKO and stromal Stat3-sKO)
conflicting: none; the question is whether mouse compartment genetics licenses a human-model node
current: E_GP130_STAT3 is an exact alias of E_LIF and of OUT_EPITHELIAL_RECEPTIVE
proposed: A stromal pathway component with its own downstream route
impact: would break the E_LIF/E_GP130_STAT3/OUT_EPITHELIAL_RECEPTIVE alias class, which is currently why this axis cannot be calibrated
strength: mouse in vivo, conditional and compartment-specific; indirect for the ADOC
observability: E_GP130_STAT3 is the only one of the five audited targets visible in both clamp directions today
identifiability: a stromal node would need a stromal readout the ADOC does not measure

title: Temporal LIF signalling
issue: Early glandular and later stromal LIF are distinct in mouse; one static epithelial node collapses both source and timing.
current: E_LIF sits in an alias class with E_GP130_STAT3 and OUT_EPITHELIAL_RECEPTIVE
proposed: Phase-dependent inputs or timed interventions rather than new nodes
affects: semantics and protocol timing, not topology
impact: unknown without simulation; the protocol layer already supports step-level interventions (O8a)
observability: no timed LIF readout in the ADOC
identifiability: timing differences are exactly what fixed-point analysis cannot see
readiness: investigable now via the protocol layer, without touching the network
approval: owner; protocol-level work may not need the pause lifted

title: MUC1 abundance versus barrier function
issue: The node name says barrier, the evidence attached to it measures abundance, and the human data say glycosylation. CIT-036/CIT-037 and the audit read the same two papers oppositely because of this.
conflicting: the two readings conflict with each other, not the papers
current: E_MUC1_BARRIER is an exact alias of E_PODXL and E_DAG1_FULL
proposed: Split abundance from accessible antiadhesive function, or rename the node to what its evidence measures
impact: would change which citations support or contradict five edges
strength: two human studies, descriptive and cell-line respectively
observability: MUC1 is not among the two measured ADOC readouts
identifiability: abundance and function are not separable by any current readout
readiness: blocked on the owner decision, not on evidence
approval: owner; this is the blocking decision for R3-015 and R3-016

title: Decidualization markers are the same function
issue: PRL and IGFBP1 can mark different subpopulations, including stressed or senescent stroma. In this model they are the identical Boolean function.
current: S_PRL, S_IGFBP1, S_SPP1, S_TAZ_ECM, S_DECIDUALIZED and OUT_STROMAL_DECIDUALIZED are one alias class
proposed: Distinguish at least PRL from IGFBP1 downstream of S_DECIDUALIZED
new_nodes: no, but their rules would have to differ
affects: topology and the meaning of the one measured stromal readout
impact: S_IGFBP1 is one of only two measured nodes, so today the ADOC stromal readout is indistinguishable from the decidualization output itself
observability: S_IGFBP1 is measured; S_PRL is not
identifiability: no experiment reading only OUT_STROMAL_DECIDUALIZED can separate them

title: Mechanical endpoints are not interchangeable
issue: Stromal Young's modulus, ECM stiffness, initial attachment, retention and spheroid expansion are distinct endpoints the module treats as one.
conflicting: none; the issue is endpoint conflation
current: X_MECHANICAL_PERMISSIVE_ECM = IN_PROGESTIN and IN_cAMP and not(stress)
proposed: Separate the attachment-time endpoints before adding mechanism
impact: unknown; three assessments on these edges remain unverifiable by text alone
strength: one human primary nanomechanics study, one partly-mouse causal study
observability: no mechanical readout in the ADOC
identifiability: S_TAZ_ECM is visible only on loss, not on gain

title: Three declared inputs have no downstream effect
issue: All three are self-referential and read by no rule, so setting them changes nothing. Any protocol arm that varies them is a structural null.
supporting: structural fact of network.bnd, confirmed by load_structure
current: each node's rule is itself; unread_inputs reports all three
proposed: Document as inert, or give them effects only through an approved change (MCC-01 would give two of them one)
impact: none until an effect is added; documenting prevents a null being read as a negative result
readiness: documentation ready now; effects are MCC-01
